title: Ghostlands
body: South of the Elrendar River, the forests of Quel'Thalas give way to the Ghostlands, a country that never recovered from the Third War. When Arthas led the Scourge north toward Silvermoon and the Sunwell, his host left a blighted trail of death behind it, and that trail, the Dead Scar, still runs from the citadel of Deatholme across the heart of the region. The survivors of that onslaught named the ruined land the Ghostlands, and the name has proven all too apt. Ghosts haunt the abandoned villages, plague runs in the blood of lynx, bat and spider, and even the murlocs of the coast walk in undeath. From Deatholme the traitor Dar'Khan Drathir commands what remains of the Scourge. Against him stand the blood elves of Tranquillien, aided by Forsaken soldiers sent by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the magisters of the Sanctum of the Sun and the Farstriders of Lake Elrendar. To the east, Shadowpine trolls of the Amani hold the forest along the road to Zul'Aman.

title: Tranquillien
body: Tranquillien was a high elven town until the fall of Quel'Thalas, when its people abandoned it and retreated to Silvermoon. Now it is the blood elves' foothold in the Ghostlands, ringed by enemies and short of nearly everything. Dame Auriferous governs the town, while Forsaken soldiers under High Executor Mavren hold the tower on its western side, a sight that still unsettles some of the sin'dorei. Dragonhawks carry supplies down from Silvermoon, where even the merchants admit that the Forsaken have put their backs to the wall for the elves, and a trader in town grumbles about an escort that never came. From here the campaign against Dar'Khan is planned, argued over and launched.

title: Goldenmist Village
body: Goldenmist Village lies in the northwest of the Ghostlands, reached by the western road out of Tranquillien. It was a high elven village until the Scourge came, and its people never truly left: the elves who died there returned as ghosts and wraiths that still drift through the empty houses, a gruesome tactic the Scourge seems to favor. Tranquillien counts freeing it the second step in its campaign to break the Scourge hold on the outlying villages. Atop its central building is a rune of summoning, where young warlocks of Silvermoon are sent to call forth a voidwalker and defeat it before returning to their teachers.

title: Sanctum of the Moon
body: West of Tranquillien stand the remains of the Sanctum of the Moon, an arcane sanctum of old Quel'Thalas. While the magisters pour their effort into the rebuilt Sanctum of the Sun, this one has been all but forgotten. Little of the structure survives, and the energies that still linger in it have given rise to bizarre creatures: arcane devourers and mana shifters that feed among the ruins. Magister Darenis of Tranquillien, who hates to see good resources go to waste, wants the crystallized mana essences these creatures carry, and he finds them remarkably powerful.

title: Suncrown Village
body: In the northeastern Ghostlands, west of Lake Elrendar, lie the ruins of Suncrown Village. Its people once held a yearly rite to keep the forces of nature under their control, and dominion over water was symbolized by summoning and binding an elemental called Aquantion. The rite ended in disaster, and the drowned villagers haunt the lake still. Since the Scourge invasion, nerubians have claimed the village, and their guards swarm its broken streets. It is the first of the outlying villages Tranquillien means to win back, and among the ruins a blood elf sent to clear it lies dying.

title: Lake Elrendar
body: Lake Elrendar spreads across the northeast of the Ghostlands, not far from the Elrendar River that divides this land from Eversong. Its waters offer no refuge. Vengeful and ravening apparitions drift over the surface, the spirits of elves who drowned there in a tragedy whose details are now mostly forgotten, and on the lake bed lies the Altar of Tidal Mastery, where the people of Suncrown once bound the elemental Aquantion. On the western shore the survivors of a failed Farstrider attack on the trolls across the water nurse their wounds, while the Farstrider Enclave keeps watch from the southern bank.

title: Dawnstar Spire
body: On the eastern shore of Lake Elrendar rises Dawnstar Spire, the tower where Dar'Khan Drathir spent much of his time while he still lived, passing many nights there scheming against his own people, and every elf knows of his plan to steal the power of the Sunwell for the Scourge. Arcane reavers now guard its halls. Ranger Vynna of the Farstrider Enclave hopes the traitor left something of himself behind, a journal or notes, that might yet be turned against him.

parts.body: Among the dust lay a journal, and its first pages leave no doubt that it was Dar'Khan's. Whoever turns them is gripped by an unnerving sense of being watched. They are full of hatred and contempt for his own people, his machinations and plots recorded in careful detail, and Ranger Vynna may well find something of use in them.

title: Farstrider Enclave
body: The Farstrider Enclave stands on the southern shore of Lake Elrendar, cut off from the other blood elf holdings and hemmed in by haunted water to the north and Shadowpine trolls to the east and south. Captain Helios commands the rangers here, and they have spent their strength keeping the trolls off balance rather than marching on Deatholme, a choice the Forsaken commander in Tranquillien calls senseless skirmishing. An apothecary on loan from Tranquillien brews poisons for the trolls' food, and a wanted poster offers a reward for the head of Kel'gash the Wicked, chieftain of the Shadowpine.

title: The Shadowpine Villages
body: The Shadowpine, a forest troll tribe of the Amani, hold three camps in the eastern Ghostlands. Zeb'Sora lies on the far shore of Lake Elrendar, where a Farstrider attack ended in slaughter. Zeb'Tela, east of the Farstrider Enclave, shelters headhunters and shadowcasters, and Zeb'Nowa to the south straddles both sides of the road to Zul'Aman and is home to the tribe's catlords and hexxers. Their chieftain, Kel'gash the Wicked, dwells there among racks of drying meat and fish. Backed by the might of Zul'Aman, these camps keep the Farstriders from turning their full strength against the Scourge.

title: The Dead Scar
body: The Dead Scar is the trail of ruin Arthas Menethil left across Quel'Thalas as he marched on Silvermoon and the Sunwell. Beginning at Deatholme, it runs north through the heart of the Ghostlands and over the river into Eversong, a ribbon of blighted, lifeless ground. Mindless Scourge still follow it to this day: risen hungerers, gangled cannibals and dreadbone skeletons wander its length, and the abomination Luzran stalks among them. Two Scourge ziggurats rise in the middle of the Scar. Even the roads that cross it are dangerous; the trader Rathis Tomber lost a supply cart to ghouls just beyond it on his way to Tranquillien.

title: An'daroth, An'telas and An'owyn
body: Three old ley-line nexuses of the high elves lie scattered across the Ghostlands: An'daroth to the northwest beyond the Dead Scar, An'telas on the southern slopes of Sungraze Peak, and the remote An'owyn far to the south. Night elves have come to them. Sentinel spies hold An'daroth and infiltrators guard An'owyn, and beside them stand strange objects like small, magically grown trees with glowing orbs atop them. At An'telas, where Magister Sylastor studies the nexus energy for use against the Scourge, the bodies of a night elf party lie about the nexus.

parts.body: The strange trees are moon crystals. Sylastor cut down the night elves at An'telas with scouts and casters from the Sanctum of the Sun, and from their stolen plans he has learned what the crystals are: scrying devices, meant to spy on the sin'dorei. An'daroth lacks the power to drive them, but An'owyn has more than enough.

title: Sanctum of the Sun
body: Southeast of Tranquillien, just south of Sungraze Peak, the magisters have rebuilt an old arcane sanctum and put it back in working order. The Sanctum of the Sun is a banner of defiance raised before Dar'Khan's seat of power, and some of Silvermoon's most powerful magisters have come to run it under Magister Kaendris. Here they study the Scourge's weaknesses with the help of the Forsaken and prepare the assault on Deatholme. Patience runs thin. Magister Idonis chafes at every delay, while Arcanist Janeda reminds him that working sanctums are rare, and that once this one runs at full capacity Silvermoon will have to send help.

title: Sungraze Peak and the Amani Catacombs
body: Sungraze Peak rises east of Tranquillien, and within it lie the Amani Catacombs, where the forest trolls laid their dead to rest. The dead do not rest there now. Mummified headhunters have begun to rise and walk the tunnels, some carrying juju, glowing objects that house an unknown power, and Shadowpine oracles move among them. Tranquillien wants the remains that have not yet stirred put to the torch. The trolls use the catacombs for captives as well. A Farstrider, Ranger Lilatha, was ambushed and locked in a cage there, certain that her captors mean to sacrifice her.

title: Underlight Mines
body: The Underlight Mines lie southwest of Tranquillien, reached by a short dirt track off the southern road just past one of the ziggurats. Their ore is a strategic asset in the campaign, for the armor and weapons the defenders need must first be dug from the ground. A clan of gnolls calling themselves the Blackpaw has overrun the tunnels and driven the miners out. Apprentice Shatharia, sent from the Sanctum of the Sun to gather tin and copper samples for an experiment against the Scourge, waits at the entrance wondering how she is to finish her errand with gnoll vermin everywhere.

title: The Twin Ziggurats
body: In the middle of the Dead Scar stand the Bleeding Ziggurat and the Howling Ziggurat, twin Scourge structures held by darkmages of Deatholme and stonewing trackers. High Executor Mavren counts them the only ground that must be secured before a strike at the Tower of the Damned. The abomination Knucklerot patrols near the Howling Ziggurat, and Tranquillien has posted a bounty for his head and that of his fellow abomination, Luzran, both dreadful creations of Dar'Khan.

parts.body: Dar'Khan's own journal reveals why the ziggurats matter. He promised his masters two elven artifacts, the stone of light and the stone of flame, charged with the energies of the Sunwell and attuned to ward against the Scourge, and the stones were to be carried to the very ground where the ziggurats now stand.

title: Windrunner Village
body: Windrunner Village, in the southwest of the Ghostlands, was the last and hardest of the three outlying villages Tranquillien set out to reclaim. Here the Scourge posted not mindless dead but its stronger shock troops: phantasmal shades drifting among the houses and stonewing gargoyles stalking the lanes. The magisters of the Sanctum of the Sun have taken a keen interest in their remains, hoping that study of them will reveal new ways of fighting the Scourge. Nearby stands Windrunner Spire, the ancestral home of the family that gave Quel'Thalas its most famous rangers.

title: Windrunner Spire
body: Windrunner Spire was the family seat of the Windrunners and the original home of Sylvanas Windrunner, once ranger-general of Quel'Thalas and now queen of the Forsaken. The mindless Scourge hold it today. Deatholme acolytes and the risen bodies of fallen rangers walk its grounds, cultists and dead elves defiling the house of the woman who once led her homeland's defense. The Forsaken of Tranquillien count its recapture an honor. Among the undead there, a shimmering necklace has turned up, a piece the gloom of the Ghostlands never seems to dim.

title: Deatholme
body: Deatholme is the Scourge citadel in the southwest of the Ghostlands, where the Dead Scar begins. From the Tower of the Damned at its heart Dar'Khan Drathir rules the undead of the region, served by four lieutenants: Masophet the Black, Jurion the Deceiver, Borgoth the Bloodletter and Mirdoran the Fallen. Nerubian centurions, wailers and eyes of Dar'Khan guard its paths, and the fortress has only one way in or out. Prisoners taken here are tortured under will-breaking poisons. Near the tower lies the body of Blood Knight Dawnstar, who led a failed assault, and a Scourge creature called Dr. Whitherlimb roams the area, harvesting fresh parts and organs for his abominations.

title: Hatchet Hills and the Amani Pass
body: In the eastern Ghostlands the land climbs through the Hatchet Hills toward the Amani Pass, the gateway to the troll city of Zul'Aman. At the foot of the pass stands the camp of the treasure hunter Budd Nedreck, complete with a flight master, provisioners and a crew of hangers-on, while the corpses of troll catlords and hexxers lie scattered around it. Budd's own bodyguards hold the road up into the pass.

title: Dar'Khan Drathir
body: Dar'Khan Drathir was a magister of Quel'Thalas who spent long nights in Dawnstar Spire and came to despise his own people. When Arthas marched north, Dar'Khan pledged himself to the Scourge, helped it slip past the kingdom's defenses and plotted to steal the power of the Sunwell for his new masters. The death knight later slew him, yet he is believed to have returned from the dead, and from the Tower of the Damned in Deatholme he now commands the Scourge of the Ghostlands. Lady Sylvanas has her own history with him and wants him dead as much as the elves do.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/Dar'Khan_Drathir (helped Arthas slip through Thalassian defenses; killed by the death knight per Arthas: Rise of the Lich King)

parts.body: His journal, found at Dawnstar Spire, held more than hatred. To the Scourge he had promised two elven treasures, the stone of light and the stone of flame, imbued with the power of the Sunwell and attuned to ward against the undead, and if they can still be found, that power could serve against the masters he chose.
sources: quest 9176 description (promised the Scourge the stones of light and flame; greatly useful in our struggle)

parts.body: His second life did not last. In the Tower of the Damned the traitor was struck down at last, and the Scourge of the Ghostlands lost the master who had commanded them from Deatholme.
sources: creature 16329 Dar'Khan Drathir in Deatholme
quest 9167 completion and reward text

title: High Executor Mavren
body: High Executor Mavren commands the Forsaken at Tranquillien. Lady Sylvanas appointed him to help the blood elves destroy Dar'Khan because he has fought the Scourge before, and he never lets anyone forget it. In the tower on the town's west side he argues his case to Dame Auriferous again and again: Deatholme has only one way in and out, the villages and the trolls are distractions, and a single focused blow at the Tower of the Damned would bring down the rest of the Scourge like a body without its head. He admits that the Undercity is stretched thin and can spare few more. The Forsaken, he says, are the reinforcements.
sources: warcraft.wiki.gg/wiki/High_Executor_Mavren (appointed by Sylvanas to assist Auriferous because he had fought the Scourge)

title: Dame Auriferous
body: Dame Auriferous governs Tranquillien for Silvermoon, grateful for her Forsaken allies yet impatient for the soldiers their Lady promised. She refuses to throw blood elf lives away on a headlong assault. Her plan is to reclaim the surrounding villages first and cut Deatholme off from reinforcement, for she will not march on Dar'Khan with Shadowpine trolls arrayed along her eastern border and enemies at her back. Advisor Valwyn whispers counsel in her ear and warns visitors that an audience may mean a long wait, and even in a war zone the dame expects the chef she brought from Silvermoon to serve her meals with a proper crunch.
sources: creature_text 16231 (all groups: villages first; lives are blood elf; Your Lady promised us more soldiers; Shadowpine and Zul'Aman on the eastern border; Deatholme must come last)

title: Arcanist Vandril
body: Arcanist Vandril directs the fight against the Scourge from Tranquillien. He has learned through hard experience that the undead can only be beaten back in small steps, since every defender who falls may rise again in their ranks, and that no mistakes can be afforded along the way. Tranquillien is surrounded, the outlying villages overrun, and Vandril means to win them back one after another, Suncrown, Goldenmist and Windrunner, sending volunteers out to retake each in turn, for Quel'Thalas, he insists, must be reclaimed.
sources: quest 9139 request text (beaten back in small steps; they add your fallen to their ranks)

parts.body: Word from the capital came at last. A courier brought a letter from Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron, an answer Tranquillien had awaited for weeks, and it warned of a dark presence in the Ghostlands. Vandril could only remark that he might have told the regent that himself.

parts.body: Suncrown proved worse than his scouts had reported. Its nerubians had a leader, Anok'suten, of whom no scouting mission had said a word, and Vandril apologized for the shoddy intelligence: his people are spread too thin, and things are slipping through the cracks.
sources: quest 9315 completion and reward text

title: Magister Kaendris
body: Magister Kaendris leads the magisters of the Sanctum of the Sun. He holds that the Ghostlands will not be won back by military force alone, and that the guile and arcane learning of his order will tip the balance. While his colleague Idonis frets at the delay and asks why Kaendris will not yet move against Dar'Khan, Kaendris waits on what the Farstriders have uncovered, for magisters and rangers may not always see eye to eye, but on Dar'Khan they agree: a way must be found to defeat him.
sources: gossip 16239 (not by military force alone; guile and knowledge of the arcane)

parts.body: What the Farstriders uncovered was a book, and Kaendris knew the handwriting at once: it was Dar'Khan's own. Somewhere in its pages, he judged, lay a weakness in their enemy, and the rangers had shown great wisdom in leaving the matter in the magisters' hands.
sources: quest 9172 reward text

parts.body: The journal told of the stone of light and the stone of flame, charged with the Sunwell's energies, and Kaendris had them taken from the twin ziggurats. Through them he means to turn the traitor's own ambition into his undoing, vanquishing Dar'Khan with the very power he sought to steal.

title: Captain Helios
body: Captain Helios commands the Farstriders at their enclave on Lake Elrendar, and for now his war is with the Shadowpine trolls rather than the Scourge. He means to cut their numbers down and break them before turning toward Deatholme, and meanwhile his rangers keep the trolls off balance, bringing back their weapons for use against the undead. He has put a price on the head of their chieftain, Kel'gash the Wicked, and with his resources spread thin he welcomes every volunteer who comes to the enclave.

parts.body: The campaign has cost him dearly. He trusted Lieutenant Tomathren to lead the attack on Zeb'Sora and admits he badly overestimated the man, and he has sent a group to bring Tomathren and Valanna safely in. Ranger Salissa, sent south to beg for help, never arrived, and he fears the worst.

parts.body: Not every lost ranger is lost for good. Ranger Lilatha came home alive from her cage in the Amani Catacombs, and Helios, thanking her rescuer, had her injuries seen to, though he sighs that the catacombs must now be cleared as well, as if the living trolls were not trouble enough.

title: Ranger Valanna and Lieutenant Tomathren
body: On the shore of Lake Elrendar wait the survivors of a disastrous Farstrider expedition. Lieutenant Tomathren rushed his rangers into battle with the trolls of Zeb'Sora without scouting first, and many died. He has since come apart, insisting it was not his fault, expecting a commendation one moment and mistaking the lakeshore for Silvermoon the next. Ranger Valanna, badly wounded, is left to nursemaid him. She sent two rangers running for help, one to Tranquillien and one to the Farstrider Enclave, and while she waits she trades insults with her commander and asks for troll ears to string into a necklace in revenge.

title: Geranis Whitemorn
body: Geranis Whitemorn was one of the people of Suncrown Village and lingers on a small island in Lake Elrendar, one of its restless dead. Each year the villagers held a rite to bind the water elemental Aquantion as a sign of their dominion over nature, but through a wicked perversion of their magic the elemental broke his bonds and enslaved them instead. Geranis seeks the wave-shaped medallions the celebrants once wore, now lost on the lake bed, so that the spirits of the drowned of Suncrown may be freed.

Laid at the Altar of Tidal Mastery on the lake bed, the medallions will summon him again, and this time he must be destroyed.

title: Kel'gash the Wicked
body: Kel'gash the Wicked is chieftain of the Shadowpine, the forest trolls whose camps fill the eastern Ghostlands. He dwells in Zeb'Nowa, the tribe's camp astride the road to Zul'Aman, where his catlords and hexxers live, and his warriors cut down many Farstriders at Zeb'Sora while Shadowpine oracles move among the mummified dead of the Amani Catacombs. Captain Helios has posted a wanted notice promising a reward for the chieftain's head, no questions asked, though no advances.

title: Budd Nedreck
body: Budd Nedreck is a human adventurer, a famous one by his own account, who has made camp in the Hatchet Hills at the very gates of Zul'Aman. His inscrutable theories, he insists, confirm rumors of vast treasure within the troll city, with mounts and mansions for everyone. Budd prefers that others take the risks. The recruits he lent his precious map to went missing while hunting the troll beast Nalorakk, and now he wants anyone hungry for fame and fortune to go in after it, promising they will go down in history as the ones who helped him unlock the secrets of Zul'Aman.

parts.body: Budd's promises had limits. Once his helpers, wearing his hand-crafted disguises, had scouted the city and dispatched the Hex Lord Malacrass himself, he declared the light work done and let them go, their potential reached, he said, if not far exceeded, so that he alone could make yet another mark on history.

parts.body: When the blood of Zul'jin himself was brought to him, Budd struggled to hide his dismay. He could have taken the warlord with ease, he sniffed; the legends are overstated, and the pitiful old cretin was more likely overcome with arthritis. He called it the least that could be done in payment for his kindness.
sources: quest 11178 completion and reward text

title: A Letter for Tranquillien
body: The road into the Ghostlands begins with a missing messenger. Courier Dawnstrider was sent south from Eversong a few days ago on an errand of an extremely secret nature, and he never returned. His aunt, Magistrix Landra Dawnstrider of Fairbreeze Village, fears the worst. A missing messenger might mean little to the callous magisters of Silvermoon, she says, but he is like a son to her, and she begs a stranger to look for him on the road toward the Ghostlands, where the beasts south of the river carry plague in their blood.
sources: quests 9144, 9147, 9148 (descriptions, request and reward texts)

parts.body: He was found by the road near the bridge over the Elrendar River, collapsed and barely conscious. He gasped that he must reach Tranquillien and could not fail, and then his eyes went blank once more.

sources: quest 9147 description and reward text

parts.body: Too weak to go on, the courier handed over his burden: a letter from Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron to Arcanist Vandril in Tranquillien. After weeks of waiting the town had its answer from the capital at last. The regent sensed a dark presence in the Ghostlands, which, Vandril observed dryly, nobody in Tranquillien needed to be told.
sources: quest 9148 description and reward text

title: The Forsaken and the Three Villages
body: Tranquillien's newest allies are walking corpses. The Forsaken of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, herself born in these lands, have come to the Ghostlands because they share an enemy with the blood elves: Dar'Khan the traitor. Their commander, High Executor Mavren, assures newcomers that his people mean the sin'dorei no harm. The partnership is not an easy one. Mavren would strike straight at Deatholme, while Dame Auriferous insists on first reclaiming the outlying villages to choke off the Scourge's reinforcements, and the final decision is hers. So Arcanist Vandril sends volunteers northeast to Suncrown Village to break the nerubians, then northwest to Goldenmist, taken by the ghosts of its own people, and at last southwest to Windrunner Village and its shades and gargoyles.
sources: quests 9327, 9329 (descriptions and reward texts)
quests 9758, 9138, 9139, 9140, 9315 (descriptions and reward texts)

parts.body: Suncrown held a surprise. A blood elf sent to clear it lay dying among the ruins, and with his last strength he told of a leader no scouting mission had reported: Anok'suten, who wanders the village at the head of its nerubians.
sources: quest 9315 description and completion text

parts.body: Windrunner Village fell last. With its shades and gargoyles thinned and their remains bound for the magisters, the Scourge hold on all three villages is broken, and Tranquillien can at last focus its forces on the Dead Scar and south toward Deatholme.
sources: quest 9140 description and reward text

title: Eyes Upon the Sin'dorei
body: Not every intruder in the Ghostlands serves the Scourge. Dame Auriferous has learned that night elves have taken over an island off the coast and set up a small camp at An'daroth, an old high elf ley-line nexus northwest of Tranquillien, reached by a dirt path just past the Dead Scar. She wants to know what they are up to there, and in the meantime she would have as many of the conceited night elves slain as can be managed.
sources: quests 9160, 9163, 9166, 9169 (descriptions and reward texts)
gameobjects 181138, 181139, 181140 (night elf plans on Shalandis Isle)

parts.body: At An'daroth there were only Sentinel spies and strange objects like small, magically grown trees crowned with glowing orbs. With the night elves' plans not readily apparent, Auriferous chose a more direct course: a raid on Shalandis Isle, just off the western coast, and the night elf ship there, to steal whatever plans could be found.

quest 9163 description

parts.body: The stolen plans were troubling. They showed night elf forces at An'daroth and also at An'owyn, a more remote nexus, but said nothing of a third nexus to the east, An'telas, where Magister Sylastor studies the ley energies for use against the Scourge. Auriferous wanted the plans taken to him.
sources: quest 9163 reward text
quest 9166 description

parts.body: Sylastor had trouble of his own: night elves had conjured a moon crystal at An'telas, and he had only just cut them down with scouts and casters from the Sanctum of the Sun. Reading the plans, he understood. The moon crystals are scrying devices, and An'owyn holds power enough to let the night elves spy on every move the sin'dorei make.
sources: quest 9166 reward text
quest 9169 description

parts.body: With a controlling orb taken from one of the infiltrators, the moon crystal at An'owyn was shut down. Sylastor was greatly relieved: surrounded by enemies as the sin'dorei are, at least none of them can now watch their every move.
sources: quest 9169 reward text

title: The Shadowpine War
body: The Farstriders of Lake Elrendar fight a war of their own against the Shadowpine trolls, who are backed by the might of Zul'Aman and hold the forest along Quel'Thalas's eastern border. It began badly: an attack on Zeb'Sora under Lieutenant Tomathren was launched without scouting, and many rangers died. Since then Captain Helios has kept the trolls off balance, sending volunteers against the headhunters and shadowcasters of Zeb'Tela and the catlords and hexxers of Zeb'Nowa, and bringing back their weapons for use against the Scourge. An apothecary on loan from Tranquillien poisons the trolls' food, and their chieftain, Kel'gash the Wicked, has a price on his head. Inside Sungraze Peak the troll dead of the Amani Catacombs have begun to rise, and Tranquillien orders the remains burned.

parts.body: The rising dead are no accident. Shadowpine oracles are raising the mummies with glowing juju in their reanimation rites, bolstering the tribe's numbers through necromantic means, and Tranquillien wants proof of the final demise of every one.

parts.body: The harassment has worked. After the assaults on Zeb'Tela and Zeb'Nowa there are, by all accounts, not many trolls left, and the Farstriders have the breathing room they need to build up their forces, and perhaps, at last, to join Tranquillien against Deatholme. Only with the trolls broken, the rangers have always said, could they turn south.
sources: quest 9277 reward text
quest 9214 description and reward text

parts.body: Kel'gash's head has reached Captain Helios. With their chieftain dead and their numbers decimated, the Shadowpine should be in total disarray, and Helios sees the perfect opportunity for the counter-offensive that will wipe them out for good.
sources: quest 9215 reward text

title: The Traitor's Destruction
body: From Tranquillien the war turns south. Some of Silvermoon's most powerful magisters have rebuilt the Sanctum of the Sun on the enemy's doorstep, and they plan an offensive into Deatholme, Dar'Khan's stronghold. Magister Idonis sends volunteers to fight the nerubians, wailers and eyes of Dar'Khan that hold the fortress, while Magister Kaendris waits on the Farstriders, for magisters and rangers agree that a way must be found to defeat the traitor. At the Farstrider Enclave, Ranger Vynna sends searchers to Dawnstar Spire, where Dar'Khan once hid to scheme against his own people, in hope of any notes he left behind.
sources: quests 9151, 9220, 9170, 9877, 9164 (descriptions and reward texts)
quests 9161, 9162, 9172, 9282, 9176, 9167 (descriptions and reward texts)
notes: Converted: the lieutenants and the prisoners moved to part 1 (QUEST_DONE 9220, which opens 9170 and 9877); the journal to part 2 (QUEST_DONE 9162); the stones to part 3 (QUEST_DONE 9176); Dar'Khan's death to part 4 (QUEST_DONE 9167). Lor'themar's reaction to the head (quests 9328, 9811) dropped: it opens the Envoy to the Horde chain, which silvermoon.json 348712 owns. Earlier: Faction 2: all quests Horde-only. The wiki's note that Dar'Khan's death let the blood elves join the Horde as equals was left out of the body (not stated in 3.3.5 text beyond Lor'themar's hint). Check: part 4 regains the head sent on to Lor'themar (quest 9328, 9811 descriptions, offered by Kaendris at the 9167 turn-in); his reaction stays with silvermoon.json 348712.

parts.body: The Scourge have felt the sanctum's wrath, and with their numbers weakened Idonis turns to strategic targets: the traitor's four lieutenants, Masophet the Black, Jurion the Deceiver, Borgoth the Bloodletter and Mirdoran the Fallen. Arcanist Janeda arranges the rescue of prisoners held in Deatholme under will-breaking poisons, with a restorative draught from Tranquillien's apothecary.
sources: quest 9220 reward text
quest 9170 description
quests 9877, 9164 descriptions

parts.body: Dawnstar Spire gave up Dar'Khan's journal, its pages full of hatred and contempt for his own people and his plots set down in great detail. Everyone knew of his plan to steal the Sunwell's power for the Scourge, but much in it was new, and Vynna sent it on to Magister Kaendris.
sources: quest 9162 description and reward text

parts.body: Kaendris knew the handwriting at once. The journal told of two elven artifacts promised to the Scourge, the stone of light and the stone of flame, imbued with the Sunwell's energies and carried to where the twin ziggurats now stand on the Dead Scar. Recovered at last, they will vanquish Dar'Khan with the very power he sought to steal.
sources: quest 9172 reward text
quest 9176 description and reward text

parts.body: Armed with the stones, a champion of Tranquillien entered Deatholme and slew Dar'Khan in his tower. The traitor's fall dealt a deadly blow to the Scourge's grip on the region, and Kaendris foresees the day, not long off, when the elves have reclaimed their lands and their greatness is restored. The traitor's head was to go on to Regent Lord Lor'themar Theron in Silvermoon City, the start of a new chapter for the sin'dorei.
sources: quest 9167 description and reward text
quests 9328, 9811 descriptions (take the traitor's head to Lor'themar Theron; the beginning of a new chapter)
